sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Button looks and sizes
sections.what: Defines every button style: primary, destructive, outline, secondary, ghost (almost invisible) and link (underlined text), plus four sizes including a square icon size. It also adds a small hover and press effect.
sections.why: Keeps every style decision in one place so buttons match across the app.
sections.watch_out: The variant and size names are used by other files, so renaming one breaks those callers.

sections.name: ButtonProps
sections.title: Button component
sections.what: Draws the button with the chosen look and passes other attributes through. If the asChild setting is on, the look is applied to the child element instead of a real button.
sections.why: Lets a link look like a button without nesting a button inside a link.
sections.watch_out: No default type is set, so inside a form the button submits by default.

summary: The main clickable button used across the app, in six looks and four sizes.
purpose: Gives every button the same look and behavior, and lets pages pick a style such as outline or destructive.
why: Likely reason: a shared button so the whole app matches. Reason not stated for most individual choices. Comments with a platform tag describe edits from the standard version.
how: Step 1: Defines the looks (primary, destructive, outline, secondary, ghost, link) and the sizes (default, small, large, icon). Step 2: Builds the button component, which draws either a real button or another element the page chooses. Step 3: Exports the button and its style definitions.
inputs: The label or icon inside, an optional variant and size, an optional asChild setting, and any normal button attributes.
outputs: A clickable button on screen in the chosen style and size.
risks: No default button type is set, so a button placed inside a form submits that form when clicked unless the page sets a type. Renaming a variant or size breaks any page that uses the old name.
debug: If a button looks wrong, check the variant and size values and whether the page overrides classes. If clicking submits a form unexpectedly, add a type to that button. If asChild is used, make sure the child element can accept the styling.
